blocks.text: 73 קְרִיאַת הַתּוֹרָה לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 73
Before reading from the Torah, the individual called upon says the following:
בָּרְכוּ אֶת־יְיָ הַמְבֹרָךְ׃
Cong. בָּרוּךְ יְיָ הַמְבֹרָךְ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד׃
He then repeats this and continues:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר בָּֽחַר־בָּֽנוּ מִכָּל־הָעַמִּים, וְֽנָֽתַן־לָֽנוּ אֶת־תּוֹרָתוֹ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה׃
uncertainties: The small vertical strokes under בָּֽחַר, בָּֽנוּ, וְֽנָֽתַן and לָֽנוּ look like metegs, but at this resolution I can't fully separate them from the kamatz stems.

blocks.text: Then the reading of the Torah begins until the end of the portion when the individual who had been called upon, says:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר נָֽתַן־לָֽנוּ תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת, וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם נָטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה׃
uncertainties: The metegs on נָֽתַן־לָֽנוּ are uncertain, for the same reason as in the blessing before the reading.

blocks.text: וקוראים בס״ת ראשון וה׳ פקד את שרה בפרשת וירא.
uncertainties: This line is in Rashi script, and the first word looks like 'וקורלים'. I read it as וקוראים (Rashi alef resembles lamed). 'לאשון' is read as ראשון.

blocks.text: וַֽיהוָ֛ה פָּקַ֥ד אֶת־שָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמָ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה לְשָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃
uncertainties: The Divine Name is printed יְהוָה / וַֽיהוָה with no holam visible.

Etnachta under אָמָ֑ר and silluq/sof pasuq at the end are clear. The conjunctive and lesser disjunctive marks (tevir, merkha, munach, darga) are visible as strokes, but at this resolution I identified them partly from their shape and position.

blocks.text: וַתַּ֩הַר֩ וַתֵּ֨לֶד שָׂרָ֧ה לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם בֵּ֖ן לִזְקֻנָ֑יו לַמּוֹעֵ֕ד אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
uncertainties: וַתַּ֩הַר֩ has a small circlet above the ת/ה area and another after the ר. There is no marginal qere note on this page, so I read these as a doubled telisha qetannah, not as qere circlets. The first circlet may sit over the ה rather than the ת.
The zaqef gadol over לַמּוֹעֵ֕ד is clear: a vertical stroke plus dots.

blocks.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶֽת־שֶׁם־בְּנ֧וֹ הַנּֽוֹלַד־ל֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־יָֽלְדָה־לּ֥וֹ שָׂרָ֖ה יִצְחָֽק׃
uncertainties: The line breaks after אֶת־ and the maqaf is printed at the line end.
The metegs on אֶֽת־, הַנּֽוֹלַד and יָֽלְדָה are faint and uncertain.
The dagesh in לּ֥וֹ is uncertain.

blocks.text: וַיָּ֤מָל אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ בֶּן־שְׁמֹנַ֖ת יָמִ֑ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
uncertainties: Postpositive pashta after אַבְרָהָם֙ is clearly visible.
The marks over and under צִוָּ֥ה are crowded, and the dots above the ו may be partly dagesh or accent.

blocks.text: לוי
uncertainties: This is a small aliyah marker printed inline before verse 5.

blocks.text: וְאַבְרָהָ֖ם בֶּן־מְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה בְּהִוָּ֣לֶד ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֥ק בְּנֽוֹ׃
uncertainties: The accent under בְּהִוָּ֣לֶד is uncertain: it could be munach or another conjunctive.

blocks.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שָׂרָ֔ה צְחֹ֕ק עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י אֱלֹהִ֑ים כָּל־הַשֹּׁמֵ֖עַ יִֽצְחַק־לִֽי׃
uncertainties: The line breaks after כָּל־ with a maqaf at the line end.
The zaqef qatan over שָׂרָ֔ה and the zaqef gadol over צְחֹ֕ק are visible.

blocks.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר מִ֤י מִלֵּל֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם הֵינִ֥יקָה בָנִ֖ים שָׂרָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי בֵ֖ן לִזְקֻנָֽיו׃
uncertainties: It's uncertain whether the plene yod in הֵינִ֥יקָה (after the נ) is printed. The glyphs are crowded.
It's uncertain whether בָנִ֖ים at the start of the line has a dagesh; it may be faint or absent.
It's uncertain whether בֵ֖ן has a dagesh.
The revia over וַתֹּ֗אמֶר and the pashta after מִלֵּל֙ are visible.

blocks.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֥ל הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַיִּגָּמַ֑ל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אַבְרָהָם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֔וֹל בְּי֖וֹם הִגָּמֵ֥ל אֶת־יִצְחָֽק׃
uncertainties: It's uncertain whether גָד֔וֹל has a dagesh; it appears to have none.

blocks.text: (בשבת ג׳)
uncertainties: This is a Rashi-script parenthetical that visually resembles '(נסנס ג.)'. I read it as בשבת ג׳, the third aliyah on Shabbat, but the last letter doesn't clearly match the ת in the rubric above. Low confidence.

blocks.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶא שָׂרָ֜ה אֶת־בֶּן־הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה
uncertainties: The verse breaks off at the bottom of the page after אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה.
The accent under יָלְדָ֥ה is uncertain: it could be merkha or another conjunctive.

notes: The biblical text is Genesis 21:1–9a, the first-day Rosh Hashanah reading, in Hebrew with full cantillation.
The Divine Name in the verses is printed יְהוָה with no visible holam. The prayers use the abbreviation יְיָ.
There are no ketiv/qere circlets with marginal notes on this page. The only circlet-like marks are on וַתַּ֩הַר֩ in 21:2, and I read them as telisha qetannah.

Some accent identities were chosen from shape and position at this scan resolution, so treat the uncertainty fields as real doubts, not boilerplate. A higher-DPI crop of lines 2–4 and 8–11 of the biblical block would settle them.
